style.notes: two tall square red-brick piers offset diagonally, each with a lower stepped shaft (stone-capped setbacks); narrow vertical slot openings; open upper bell structure (dark bronze louvred bell frame) hung between the tall piers; ground-level gap ~2 m between the piers at the centre of the base with a low plaque plinth

passages.note: open gap between the two piers (no roof until the bell frame at ~21 m); a low plaque plinth stands in it (R353, 155120)

ev.note: tower centred on the inner octagon of its base; ground footprint ~5.7 x 4.1 m from the dark mass at the base in the aerial (the top appears displaced ~(+2,+7.5) m by lean); pier arrangement and stepped heights from the oblique photos/video; total height ~28 m estimated from the base octagon (23.4 m across) in the oblique user image 155113
ev.open: exact pier sizes/offsets, setback heights and the width of the ground gap need a site measurement; height +-3 m

style.notes: compact faceted octagon: steep dark-shingle octagonal pyramid roof with a white square glazed cupola (pyramid cap); walls mostly white-framed glazing over a low red-brick base; gabled wings with white pediments (oculus) and white columns at the entries; ringed by a circular walk and crenellated low brick garden walls forming alcoves

passages.note: walk-through entry/atrium on the NE-SW axis: covered, columned, brick-paved entry passage (R013) leading to the tall glazed lobby/atrium (R011); walks reach the garden ring exactly opposite each other at NE and SW (aerial); NE gable entry seen in V02, SW portico in R009/R073. Route through the atrium assumed straight; R013 shows a plaque wall at its end, so the real route may jog around it

ev.note: core octagon and four diagonal gabled wings fitted inside the 29.6 m garden ring (inner edge r 14.8 about (70.25,25.0)); cupola top at ground (70.1,22.9) after lean correction; eave ~4.8 m and apex ~17 m estimated from R009/R355 proportions
ev.open: exact wing count/orientation (V02 shows gables on at least two sides), which entrance is the main portico, and the atrium route; footprint +-1.5 m

parts.note: portico block: white pediment with a round glazed oculus over the four giant columns, white entablature from the column tops (9.5 m) to the eave (R093, R182; lettering omitted)
white cupola on the cross gable (R093, R182)

style.notes: long 3-storey red-brick bar (89 x 13 m) with grey panels between stacked windows; centred full-height white portico of 4 columns with a pediment (oculus) on the north facade; white cupola on the cross gable; flat-roofed lounge stem and a low gravel-roofed annex on the south side

passages.note: open columned portico (4 columns, bases measured in the aerial at ~4.2 m spacing) in front of the main north door

ev.note: north and south wall lines from the visible north facade strip/eave edges along 6 cross-profiles, corrected for the measured lean (0.07,0.27) m/m; bar 89.2 m x 13.0 m at 13.05 deg; portico from the four column bases; stem/annex from the flat roofs; 3 floors counted in R093/R182
ev.open: south-side doors placed where walks/plaza meet the walls (stem east face plaza, walk ending at the bar's south wall at x~61, both ends): exact door positions unverified; stem height (8 m) from its shadow only; lobby/commons interior photos R183-R198 show lounges/kitchen but no plan

parts.note: portico block: white pediment with a round glazed oculus over the four giant columns, white entablature from the column tops (9.5 m) to the eave (R251, R267; lettering omitted)
white cupola on the cross gable (R251, R267)

style.notes: twin of the west hall: long classical 3-storey brick facade with a centred white 4-column portico and pediment on the north side, cupola on the cross gable; light flat-roofed stem and low annex on the south side

passages.note: open columned portico in front of the main north door

ev.note: wall lines from eave/facade-strip profiles at x=180,195,235,250,258 corrected for lean; bar 89.0 x 12.7 m at -17.95 deg; portico columns visible in the aerial; white flat-roofed stem and lower annex south of the centre
ev.open: side/end door positions unverified; stem height from its short shadow (~6 m)

style.notes: cluster of angular standing-seam metal roofs (hips and gables, stepped saw-tooth outline on the north-west and east), raised central light-coloured spine roof with clerestory glazing and a small rooftop cupola, red-brick walls with deep-set glazing; south-west wing rotated ~30 deg

ev.note: outline traced from the roof colour mask and 9 px/m tiles, moved by the measured lean for ~9 m eaves (-0.6,-2.4 m); parts follow the visible roof masses
ev.open: eave heights estimated from video V08 (2 storeys); entrances placed where paved forecourts meet the walls (north at the bell-tower base, south forecourt, east wing, west service side) and need photo confirmation; roof overhangs not deducted (+-1 m)

style.notes: 3-storey red-brick wings with standing-seam hip roofs; central white entrance bay with 3-storey curtain glazing and flat columned canopy (north, R108/R036); black rooftop lantern topped by a glass pyramid; green (sedum) roof terrace, flat white roof with rows of solar panels, glazed sloped atrium roof, small observatory dome and greenhouse on the south service wing; glazed link to the hexagonal annex on the west

ev.note: outline from 8-14 px/m tiles and profiles, moved by the lean for an 11 m reference height (-0.8,-3.0 m); lantern, dome, solar roof and green roof identified from R034/R035/R108
ev.open: B24/B25 split assumed: hexagonal flat-roofed block = annex (wayfinding pin 24 points at it), everything else = science center; any 2025 addition/renovation (S13) is not visible in the 2022 aerial; east entrance rotunda footprint not modelled separately

style.notes: two joined elongated hexagons with flat grey roofs, contrasting with the hipped science center; glazed atrium link on its east side

ev.note: outline from 14 px/m tile, moved by the lean for 9 m
ev.open: height (2 storeys) from its short shadow only; 2025 renovation/addition noted in the inventory could not be verified

features.note: upright dark stone pillar with a bronze bowl on top; water spills from the bowl into the basin

ev.note: small round basin on the SE edge of the walk hub west of the library: water r~1.5 m inside a ~1 m light coping ring (outer r 2.7); the pillar's 2.3 m shadow points NW; user image 155324 looks from it to the bell tower with the library close on the right, R098 shows the brick seat wall beside it
ev.open: not the jet pool listed with V03/V10 (that is the separate pool at (213,-46), traced as garden_run_pool); basin depth and rim height estimated

ev.note: round pool r 4.4 m (dark water edge in the aerial) with a central jet and a few boulders, a brown stone rim, a curved concrete walk around its north side; it is the head of the garden run: a rock cascade leaves it to the south (V03)
ev.open: rim height and depth estimated

ev.note: a stony, planted dry-creek channel meandering from the small pool by the science centre across the south lawn (dark stone band in the aerial; drawn blue on the diagrams); walks cross it
ev.open: whether it carries water except after rain; exact width (1.5-3 m) and the western end

campus loop, east side, centre from asphalt edges every 20 m

main entrance boulevard, south carriageway (in), between the east perimeter street and the loop; median island z -145..-137
main entrance boulevard, north carriageway (out); decorative light paving ovals at the crossing
turnaround drive east of the science centre
